recent_posts.title: Connect Any Git or Mercurial Repo to Pulumi with Custom VCS
recent_posts.summary: Pulumi has released Custom VCS, a new org-level integration that connects any Git or Mercurial version control system to Pulumi Deployments. It addresses gaps for teams using self-hosted or third-party VCS servers by enabling webhook-driven push-to-deploy, centralized credential management via Pulumi ESC environments, and manual repository registration. While it supports push-to-deploy and path filtering, it lacks PR previews, commit status checks, and review stacks — features that require deep API integration with specific platforms. Pulumi's AI assistant Neo can also clone and push to registered repositories using the integration's credentials.

recent_posts.title: Neo's Integration Catalog: Give Your Agent Access to the Tools It Needs
recent_posts.summary: Pulumi has launched an Integration Catalog for Neo, its infrastructure AI agent. The catalog connects Neo to six tools via the Model Context Protocol (MCP): Atlassian (Jira/Confluence), Datadog, Honeycomb, Linear, PagerDuty, and Supabase. Admins configure credentials once, and the entire team gains access without per-user setup. Credentials are encrypted at rest and decrypted only at runtime. Upcoming features include CLI tool integrations (kubectl, aws, gcloud), OAuth support for providers like Notion and Sentry, and per-team access controls for individual integrations.

recent_posts.title: Policy Packs Can Now Access Pulumi ESC Environments
recent_posts.summary: Pulumi policy packs can now reference Pulumi ESC (Environments, Secrets, and Configuration) environments, eliminating the need to hardcode credentials or configuration values in policy group configs. This enables centralized secrets management, environment-specific configuration (e.g., different thresholds for staging vs. production), dynamic credentials from cloud providers, and audit trails for credential access. The integration works by attaching an ESC environment to a policy pack within a policy group, making resolved values available at runtime via policyConfig or environment variables.

recent_posts.title: How IaC platforms can govern AI agent sprawl in production
recent_posts.summary: AI agent sprawl is a growing problem: 96% of enterprises run agents in production, but only 12% have centralized management. The post argues that IaC platforms like Pulumi already provide the seven things agents need for governance: a context lake (Pulumi state), pre-cleared integrations (ESC with OIDC dynamic credentials), governed actions (Pulumi Deployments), deterministic policy (Pulumi Policies), audit trails, review processes, and human-in-the-loop approvals. Rather than building new scaffolding, platform teams should route agent changes through the same IaC substrate already used for human changes, making the governed path the easiest path for developers.

recent_posts.title: Pulumi Cloud REST API Docs, Now Generated from OpenAPI
recent_posts.summary: Pulumi's Cloud REST API reference documentation is now auto-generated from the live OpenAPI spec at build time, replacing handwritten pages that frequently drifted out of sync. The update brings complete endpoint grouping by product area, accurate request/response schemas, and linked type navigation. Beyond human usability, the change improves reliability for AI agents that read the docs and call the API programmatically, since they now work from the actual current spec rather than potentially stale handwritten content.

recent_posts.title: Scan AWS GovCloud and more partitions with Pulumi Insights
recent_posts.summary: Pulumi Insights account scanning now supports all AWS partitions beyond standard commercial, including GovCloud (US), ISO intelligence-community clouds, European Sovereign Cloud, and China. Discovery traffic stays within each partition's boundary using partition-specific STS endpoints. Setup is done via the Pulumi Cloud console by selecting the target partition and supplying credentials through a Pulumi ESC environment with the appropriate ARN prefix.

recent_posts.title: Superpowers, GSD, and GSTACK: Picking the Right Framework for Your Coding Agent
recent_posts.summary: Three community frameworks for AI coding agents are compared: Superpowers (enforces TDD with a 7-phase workflow and subagent delegation), GSD (prevents context rot via per-phase orchestrators that write state to disk), and GSTACK (models a 23-person team with role-based governance). Each addresses a distinct failure mode: code breaking without tests, quality degrading as context windows fill, and scope creep from unchecked agent autonomy. The post maps each framework to specific use cases — Superpowers for solo devs needing test discipline, GSD for multi-day complex projects, GSTACK for founder-engineers shipping products — and discusses how they complement Pulumi infrastructure workflows.

recent_posts.title: Introducing Bun as a Runtime for Pulumi
recent_posts.summary: Pulumi now supports Bun as a fully-fledged runtime for TypeScript programs, not just as a package manager. Setting `runtime: bun` in `Pulumi.yaml` lets Bun execute Pulumi programs directly with no Node.js required, enabling native TypeScript support, faster package installs, and top-level await via ESM. The post covers how to create new Bun-based projects, migrate existing Node.js Pulumi projects (including tsconfig.json updates and ESM migration), and clarifies the difference between using Bun as a runtime vs. as a package manager only. Known limitations include lack of support for callback functions (magic lambdas) and dynamic providers, which still require Node.js. Available in Pulumi 3.227.0.

recent_posts.title: Automate Azure App Secret Rotation with ESC
recent_posts.summary: Pulumi ESC now includes an azure-app-secret rotator that automates client secret rotation for Azure App Registrations (Microsoft Entra ID). The rotator maintains current and previous secrets to ensure zero-downtime rollovers, supports configurable lifetimes up to 730 days, and can be scheduled to run before secrets expire. Setup requires an azure-login environment with appropriate Graph API permissions, and existing credentials can be seeded into the rotator's state object.

recent_posts.title: KubeCon EU 2026 Recap: The Year AI Moved Into Production on Kubernetes
recent_posts.summary: KubeCon EU 2026 in Amsterdam drew 13,350 attendees and marked a clear shift: AI workloads are moving from experimentation to production on Kubernetes. Key stats show 82% of organizations have adopted Kubernetes for AI, but only 7% deploy daily. Major themes included the pivot from training to inference (67% of AI compute now goes to inference), NVIDIA donating GPU infrastructure projects (DRA driver, KAI Scheduler, Grove) to the CNCF, and new CNCF projects like llm-d for distributed inference, kagent for agent-as-CRD, and kagenti for cryptographic agent identity via SPIFFE/SPIRE. AI gateways evolved with model-aware routing via the Gateway API Inference Extension and Envoy AI Gateway. Platform engineering teams are being urged to own AI infrastructure to prevent shadow AI sprawl, and data sovereignty under the EU Cyber Resilience Act is reshaping infrastructure architecture globally.

top_posts.title: Python for DevOps
top_posts.summary: Python is highly versatile for both quick fixes and long-term infrastructure in DevOps. It excels at building custom solutions and automating tasks using libraries like Django, Flask, Prometheus, Schedule, and Airflow. Additionally, Python supports network analysis with Scapy, security scanning with Bandit, container management with Docker SDK, and infrastructure as code with Pulumi. Combining these tools allows the efficient creation of dashboards, automations, and complex deployments from a single language.

top_posts.title: Kubernetes Best Practices I Wish I Had Known Before
top_posts.summary: Kubernetes has revolutionized the building, shipping, and running of applications, but adopting best practices can save time, money, and headaches. Key recommendations include setting resource requests and limits, using namespaces for organization, avoiding multi-container pods unless necessary, using package managers for YAML files, implementing ingress and networking best practices, and setting up proper monitoring and security measures. Additionally, it's important to automate deployments with CI/CD, keep the cluster updated, and use labels and annotations wisely. Adopting a multi-environment approach, optimizing container images, and following a reliable logging strategy further enhance efficiency and reliability.

top_posts.title: Pulumi 💜's Open Source
top_posts.summary: Pulumi is true open source, uses the Apache 2.0 license, and never will depend on BSL-licensed software in any way, HashiCorp owned or otherwise. Pulumi stands with the open source community, always with open source and our amazing, fast-growing community at our core.

top_posts.title: Host a Python app on AWS Lambda for low traffic at minimal cost
top_posts.summary: Discover how to host low-traffic Python applications on AWS Lambda for minimal cost. Using containers, developers can leverage Lambda to maintain high availability while paying only when their service is called. The post describes the process of containerizing a Flask app and deploying it with Pulumi, minimizing the need for extensive serverless knowledge. This approach allows for zero cost when idle and scalable infrastructure, benefiting APIs with sporadic traffic and cost-sensitive projects.

top_posts.title: Using Claude skills to encode DevOps expertise for infrastructure as code
top_posts.summary: Claude Skills package engineering expertise into reusable instructions that teach AI agents domain-specific patterns and best practices. Unlike MCPs which provide tools, skills encode workflows and judgment—teaching Claude to write production-ready infrastructure code with proper security contexts, monitoring, OIDC credentials, and deployment patterns. The article demonstrates 14+ community and official Pulumi skills covering TypeScript infrastructure, Kubernetes hardening, systematic debugging, security review, incident response, and SRE practices. Skills are portable markdown files that avoid context pollution through progressive disclosure, activating only when relevant. Security vetting is critical as 13.4% of public skills contain vulnerabilities.
